what_happened: The the person running Athena re-queued a fix for flaky tests that write stand-in (fake) scripts and then run them. The flakiness is an ETXTBSY error ("text file busy"). Two earlier attempts had added protection at individual run sites, and that left some runs unprotected, especially runs inside production code. The the person running Athena gave a specific design in the request: write the scripts from a child process, so the parent does not hold an inherited write handle open while another process executes the file. No job failed in this event. It is an intervention where the the person running Athena supplied the method.
cause: Athena accepts a bug request for an intermittent failure without requiring the root mechanism to be named. It also does not require a check that the fix covers every path that triggers the failure, including paths in production code that tests only reach indirectly. Each retry therefore guessed at a local patch at the places the failure was seen, and a passing run could not show the failure was gone, because the failure is intermittent. Nothing carried forward what the first two attempts left uncovered. The the person running Athena's knowledge of the mechanism (inherited write handles) was the only source of the right design.
prevention: For jobs that fix an intermittent failure, the reading and plan must name the mechanism of the failure and list every place that can trigger it, including production code. A criterion must require a deterministic reproduction or a stress run (for example, many repeated concurrent runs that fail before the change and pass after it). A retry of such a job must carry over what the earlier attempts covered and what they missed. A shared stand-in script helper that writes from a child process, used by every test and by any production code path that runs such scripts, would remove the whole class of this error.
proposed_request: Fix the flaky ETXTBSY ("text file busy") failures that occur when tests write a stand-in script and then run it. Two earlier attempts retried at individual run sites and left runs inside production code unprotected, so do not repeat that approach. Outcome: every stand-in script in the tests is created by one shared helper that writes the file from a child process, so the parent process holds no inherited write handle while the script is executed, and every test and every production code path that runs such a script goes through that helper. In the plan, name the root cause (an inherited open write handle on the file while another process executes it) and list every site that writes then runs a script. Acceptance: (1) a stress test runs the write-then-execute sequence many times concurrently and passes on every run, and the same test fails on the old approach; (2) no test or production path writes a script and executes it from the same process holding a write handle, and a check or test enforces this; (3) the full existing test suite passes; (4) edits are limited to the shared helper, the sites that use it, and tests. If any code that this change touches has a decision recorded in docs/decisions.md, add the amending or confirming entry and link it.
